title: Midnight refill re-calculation causing steady soft-throttles (429s) for multiplexed uploader
text:
Midnight refill re-calculation causing steady soft-throttles (429s) for multiplexed uploader

Issue summary: Customer reports a sustained pattern of soft 429 throttles starting shortly after midnight UTC during a scheduled bulk upload pipeline. The throttles are not spikes: they present as low-rate, persistent 429 responses across many short-lived connections used by their multiplexed uploader workers. Impact: Upload pipeline throughput drops ~25-35% for a 2–4 hour window; customers report retries and job backlogs. Environment: Dedicated pool in prod/us-east, tenant on billing tier 'dedicated' with monthly reserved capacity. Observed since 2026-03-10 after DataWeave rolled out a weekly cron that spins up ~200 short-lived worker instances and rotates ephemeral API keys every 10 minutes. Hypothesis: refill accounting and window alignment across billing refill job + edge-proxy token attribution causes token-bucket drift when many ephemeral keys are created/closed in short windows. The midnight refill (billing sweep) triggers a refactor of per-tenant refill state that briefly mis-aligns per-connection windows, effectively lowering available token capacity until background reconciliation finishes. This surfaces as persistent low-rate 429s rather than the usual microburst throttles. Steps to reproduce: 1) Configure tenant with many short-lived ephemeral keys (rotate every 10m). 2) Start multiplexed uploader that opens ~1k short streams across 200 workers. 3) Schedule a refill/credit-sweep around a small clock boundary (e.g., midnight UTC). 4) Observe 429 rate and per-connection X-RateLimit headers. Expected behaviour: consistent refill and nominal 429 spikes only on genuine exhaustion. Observed: prolonged soft-429 window for 2–4 hours after refill job.
